hook.text: A ship's captain doesn't just aim for the destination. The route is optimized around weather systems.

buildup.text: Routing services analyze wave height, wind speed, and current forecasts days ahead of the voyage.

discovery.text: The shortest route is rarely the fastest. Riding favorable currents or dodging storms can save days.

twist.text: Heavy seas don't just slow a ship—they damage cargo. A longer calm route can arrive with goods intact.

climax.text: Modern weather routing uses satellite data and AI to adjust the path continuously during the voyage.

punchline.text: Smart captains follow the weather, not the straight line.

quiz.question: Why might a ship take a longer route?
options: To dodge storms and ride favorable currents, saving time and cargo
